meta.era: Legacy Era, post-Fate of the Jedi, 47 ABY
meta.tone_description: Classic Star Wars adventure layered over genuine moral dilemma — personal stakes, tight cast, archaeological mystery building to cosmic crisis
meta.canon_status_description: A hidden-history Legends novel set in 47 ABY after Fate of the Jedi. Published continuity remains the baseline until Ben uncovers the buried Ruusan history, Veranthos, the wound, and the surviving witnesses tied to it.

positioning_statement: A close-third Ben Skywalker Legends novel that begins as an investigation and widens into a moral crisis. The prose should stay clear and propulsive while a small cast, buried history, and Force pressure gather weight scene by scene. The book should feel like a lost late-era Legends hardcover: intimate in POV, serious without grandstanding, and driven by character choice rather than thesis language.

comp_block.target_audience: Legends readers who know the broad post-NJO/FotJ shape and adult SF/F readers comfortable with moral ambiguity, institutional stakes, and close-third character work. Prior continuity knowledge should enrich the read, but first mentions must carry enough context that a reader who remembers the era more generally is never stranded.

positioning_anti_patterns: Do not signal 'Ben Skywalker adventure' in cover copy or marketing — it sets the wrong tonal expectation.
Do not imply Zahn-style political thriller — the Zahn anchor is for prose register, not for Specter-era plot architecture.
Do not use YA-adjacent framing — adult Legends readership is the target.
Do not soften the Force-metaphysical or institutional-complicity content in flap copy — the payload is the book; positioning must not bait-and-switch.
Do not invoke airport-bookstore commercial-tie-in language — that was the prior voice spec and has been retired in favor of the five-anchor architecture.

Do not lead with Veraine as a marquee Sith antagonist in the conventional sense — she is a flat-negative villain whose page-time is paced through evidence-of-passage; signalling her as 'the new Plagueis' or similar would mis-set audience expectations.

premise.what_if: What if the Ruusan Reformations carried a hidden penance for a Jedi war crime -- a forbidden technique that damaged a vergence and scarred the Force -- and a thousand years later the seal containing that wound starts to fail?
premise.central_dramatic_question: Can Ben succeed where the Jedi Lords failed — not by wielding power, but by trusting the people his Order forgot?
premise.logline: Ben Skywalker awakens three survivors of a war the Jedi Order erased from history -- and discovers they are the only people who understand the wound in the Force festering around Veranthos. With an ancient Sith racing to break the seal on her terms and his most trusted ally turning desperate enough to become the next threat, Ben must do what a thousand years of Jedi could not: find a way to contain the wound without making another person the prison.

primary_antagonistic_force.identity: Darth Veraine, Brotherhood of Darkness alchemist and strategist. Captured by Gavran's forces and repurposed as one of twelve Force-sensitive anchors in the seal's containment infrastructure. Her partial awareness during a millennium of stasis — feeling her Force presence drained as structural rebar — eroded her chamber from inside. She escaped weeks before the main cascade, her breakout accelerating the system failure that woke the remaining three survivors.
primary_antagonistic_force.motivation: The wound is real. The seal is a prison built from fear. Veraine believes Gavran's technique was a battlefield crime and that the Order compounded it by building a containment system out of living anchors, then naming that mercy. Ankhural's Codex gave her a heretical frame for what she already suspected -- that the local structure around vergences is imposed rather than natural -- and a thousand years of half-aware imprisonment turned suspicion into certainty. She intends to break the seal and accepts the transition casualties as the price of ending what the Jedi chose to preserve. Her accusation is historically accurate in key particulars; her conclusion is catastrophically wrong. She can count the bodies and still choose release. Her flaw is detachment -- she has translated suffering into arithmetic and cannot feel what the wound does to living beings strongly enough to stop.
primary_antagonistic_force.escalation: Part 1: Invisible -- referenced only through an empty stasis chamber at the fortress, broken open from inside, and monitoring logs flagging a high-risk anchor breach weeks prior. Part 2: Evidence of her passage along the Corridor's anchor nodes -- she is traveling the same route ahead of the group, repurposing each node's infrastructure into an amplification array that turns the seal's own architecture against itself. The Ash-Tithe Compact provides practical support: Vess routes and manifests, Pira technical sabotage, Serran archival/ritual authentication, Mira low-level Force calibration, plus a few disposable hired guards. Each site shows escalating sophistication. Part 3: Direct confrontation during a truce meeting (Chapter 16) where she presents her philosophy to the full group -- a three-objective operation combining ideological pitch, Kael recruitment attempt, and intelligence gathering; her crew executes a parallel sabotage out of Ben's sight, collapsing the timeline from weeks to days once the group discovers it on exit. Part 4: Full assault on the primary seal at Veranthos -- her ritual amplified by the repurposed node network, directed at the Scar. Defeated in two stages: Desh disables critical amplification nodes (physical/tactical), then the shared-burden containment Ben, Sera, and Kael establish distributes the load across willing practitioners and traditions. Veraine planned for one tradition, one authority, or one living prisoner. She did not plan for a plural answer that leaves no single person load-bearing. Contained by Sera but unbroken -- defeated by results, not by conversion.

secondary_pressures: Torin Hal (internal antagonist) — ally turned antagonist at the second plot point. His pattern mirrors Jacen Solo and the Jedi Lords: the talented, damaged Force-user who decides he alone bears responsibility for the solution. His turn is driven by desperation, not malice.

The wound itself -- reactive and destabilizing. As the seal weakens it amplifies emotional extremes in Force-sensitives nearby. Not possession, but pressurization -- every argument hits harder, every fear cuts deeper, every doubt becomes paralyzing.

The institutional lie — the Jedi Order's thousand-year cover-up of the Veranthos crime buried beneath the Reformations. Ben carries the weight of knowing the truth, and every step deeper makes it harder to imagine going home and pretending he doesn't know.

Luke's shadow — not an antagonist but a pressure. Luke sent Ben alone. The irony of that choice — sending one person to solve a problem caused by people who acted alone — becomes increasingly apparent. Ben's reluctance to call for help is both practical and personal.
conflict.lock_in_mechanism: Triple-layered: (1) The seal is failing regardless — the anchor system has been degrading for centuries as sleepers died one by one, and the final cascade has begun. Ben can't un-know what he's learned and walking away doesn't stop the collapse. (2) The survivors depend on him — they're a thousand years out of time with no resources, no allies, and no understanding of the modern galaxy. (3) Veraine is already moving — she escaped weeks before them and is systematically dismantling the seal's infrastructure along the Corridor. Even if Ben quits, she doesn't. Someone has to stop her or the wound opens on her terms.

theme.thematic_premise: People break the world when they decide they must carry the cost alone. Healing starts when they stop treating other people as burdens, tools, or witnesses.
theme.thematic_argument: Ben, Sera, Kael, Torin, and Veraine all meet the same pressure from different histories: each has been used by an institution, and each is tempted to answer crisis through control. The book keeps testing whether the wound can be faced without turning another person into structure. Ben's answer is not cleaner certainty. It is learning to let other people's judgment stand beside his own and to accept a solution no one person owns. Torin and Veraine reach for cleaner answers and pay for it.

how_each_arc_tests_theme.Ben Skywalker: Ben starts by trusting only his own read when the Force goes wrong. Each major turn forces him to rely on people whose judgment he cannot confirm for himself. By the end he is no longer trying to be the lone answer; he is holding a shared one.
how_each_arc_tests_theme.Sera Varik: Sera wakes certain that principle and discipline should have been enough to prevent Ruusan. The story keeps confronting her with the limits of being right in theory while wrong in method, until she chooses to trust without surrendering her moral core.
how_each_arc_tests_theme.Kael Drenn: Kael has survived by staying outside belief. The group only becomes real to him once people stop treating him as a category and start asking what he sees. His final choice matters because it is volunteered, not claimed by another institution.
how_each_arc_tests_theme.Torin Hal: Torin is the seductive version of noble self-sacrifice: warm, capable, sincere, and still reaching for the old pattern in which one gifted person decides the price for everyone else. His fall hurts because he is not false. He is tragically convinced.
how_each_arc_tests_theme.Darth Veraine: Veraine is right about the crime and wrong about the cure. Her pressure on the group comes from clarity, patience, and a willingness to accept casualties as arithmetic. The book never needs to soften her to defeat her.
how_each_arc_tests_theme.Desh Rolan: Desh keeps the others anchored in the world of bodies, equipment, timing, and consequence. He matters because he is present, steady, and unimpressed by mystical self-importance. When the Force-users lose their footing, he is still standing on the ground.

three_dimensions.surface: Confident, capable young Jedi Knight with a dry wit and his mother's pragmatic edge. Carries himself with an ease that reads as natural talent. People assume everything comes easy to a Skywalker. He lets them think it because correcting the assumption would require vulnerability he can't afford.
three_dimensions.backstory_inner_demons: Nothing has come easy. He was Jacen's apprentice and watched his cousin become a Sith Lord. His mother Mara was murdered by Jacen. He served in GAG — a secret police force — as a teenager. He fought in a civil war. He helped defeat Abeloth. He loved Vestara Khai, who chose the dark side and betrayed him. He's accomplished more by twenty than most Jedi manage in a lifetime, and he's exhausted by it. Underneath the competence is a young man who has never had the space to figure out who he is apart from crisis and legacy.
three_dimensions.action_under_pressure: Ben's instinct under pressure is to control — assess, plan, execute. He's his mother's son in that way. His arc forces him to learn that control is the Skywalker trap. The moments where he lets go and trusts others are the moments he wins.

weiland_arc.lie_believed: I am the only person whose read of the Force can be trusted when it's going wrong, because everyone I've trusted with that judgment has been wrong or dangerous.
weiland_arc.ghost: Jacen's fall — specifically the realization that Jacen had killed Mara. The wound that taught him the people he trusts with Force-judgment can become the threat. Compounded by Vestara's betrayal: the second person he let in with that same trust who chose the dark side.
weiland_arc.want: To read the Force correctly when it's going wrong, and to act on that read before the wrongness metastasizes the way it did with Jacen.
weiland_arc.need: To act on another person's Force-read without first verifying it against his own — and to hold the resulting coherence as a skill, not a concession. The test is not whether he can trust; it is whether he can run a read composed of judgments he cannot personally verify and treat that as the correct answer under load.
weiland_arc.arc_summary: Positive change -- moves from the Trauma Lie (only my Force-read can be trusted when the Force is going wrong) to a new truth that is measurable in specific behaviors: in Ch 21 he refuses the unilateral interdiction his Lie would have demanded; in Ch 25 s3 he holds the interpretive axis of the shared-burden containment under maximum load, composing Sera/Kael/Desh's reads into a single executable coherence he cannot verify directly; in Ch 26 s3 he takes the first public renewal share of the new seal's ongoing burden. The Legacy burden (Skywalker shadow) persists as ambient pressure throughout but is never the operative Lie -- it lives inside PP21 and Ben/Luke scenes as weather, not as the arc engine.

arc_phase_targets.lie_reinforced: Ben's lock-in convinces him the burden is his to carry because only he is reading the wrongness correctly — the survivors are witnesses, not verifiers.
arc_phase_targets.lie_questioned: The breach (Ch 13) forces the first behavioral break — the unmade Luke check-in — that is unexplained even to Ben. Ben-misreads-Torin across Chs 8-18 is the Trauma Lie under live pressure: his Force-read of whose judgment to trust is specifically what the Lie compromises, and the middle chapters render the misreading rather than correct for it.
arc_phase_targets.lie_cracking: Torin's departure (Ch 21) forces Ben to admit that the capacity the Lie told him to exercise — override another's Force-judgment when he reads them as wrong — is the exact pattern he cannot repeat. Silence is the behavior; 'we find another way, together' is the crystallisation.
arc_phase_targets.lie_confronted: At Veranthos Ben must run a Force-read composed of Sera's lock-sense, Kael's unintegrable signature, and Desh's non-sensitive operational frame — three judgments he cannot verify against his own, held as a single coherence.
arc_phase_targets.new_truth_tested: Ch 25 s3 — Ben is the interpretive axis of the resonance. He is not the reader; he is the one holding Sera, Kael, and Desh's contributions as one executable chord. If he drops the chord, the operation collapses. The Trauma-Lie antithesis demonstrated under load: trust placed in specialists whose judgment he cannot verify directly, executed as a skill he did not have in Ch 1. He holds by feel, not analysis.
arc_phase_targets.truth_resolved: Ch 26 s3 -- Ben takes the first public renewal share of the new shared-burden seal. The cost is visible, ongoing, and his, but the burden is distributed rather than prison-like; Sera and Kael witness. In Ch 28 he returns and tells Luke everything -- the private corollary to the public commitment.

arc_phase_map.lie_challenged: Chapter 13 (breach experience, unmade Luke check-in) / Chapter 18 (Jacen pattern named, Ben-misreads-Torin exposed)

ensemble_cast.name: Sera Varik
ensemble_cast.role: Conscience of the group, deuteragonist, era-specific expertise

three_dimensions.surface: Disciplined, intense, formal in a way that reads as archaic. She speaks with the gravity of someone who has never lived in peacetime. Assesses everyone tactically before engaging personally. First impression is stern, even cold. Ben initially finds her exhausting.
three_dimensions.backstory_inner_demons: She was Lord Gavran's most trusted lieutenant: a field commander, lock-breaker, and logistical conscience who believed discipline could keep wartime necessity from becoming atrocity. She argued against the Veranthos protocol before it was sealed into permanence, stayed because she thought loyal dissent still mattered, and was rewarded with removal. Gavran sealed her as one of twelve chamber-bound Force-sensitive anchors in the containment system — telling her it was 'for her own protection' — a betrayal disguised as love and command necessity. He didn't just silence her. He turned her into infrastructure, using her Force presence as structural rebar in the seal. She never got to fight at Ruusan, never got to testify, never got to stand with her comrades at the end. Underneath the discipline is someone whose deepest wound isn't war; it's that the person she trusted decided her consent was less important than his fear, and then used her body as building material.
three_dimensions.action_under_pressure: Sera's instinct is to hold the line — establish a principle and refuse to bend. This makes her reliable and maddening in equal measure. Her flaw is rigidity — she can become so committed to the 'right' answer that she can't see a better one. Her active expertise (Force-lock techniques, era-specific knowledge) makes her indispensable beyond her moral authority.

weiland_arc.lie_believed: If I had been there — if the Jedi Lord hadn't locked me away — I could have stopped all of this. Loyalty to the right principle is enough.
weiland_arc.ghost: Being sealed in stasis against her will. The moment she realized the man she followed had decided her conviction was less important than his plan.
weiland_arc.want: To finish what she started — seal the wound, honor the people who died at Ruusan, and prove that her way (restraint, principle, discipline) was right all along.
weiland_arc.need: To accept that being right about the principle doesn't mean she has all the answers — and that trusting someone new (Ben) doesn't mean repeating her mistake with Gavran.
weiland_arc.arc_summary: Positive change — moves from rigid certainty to principled flexibility, via a specific fissure at Ch 18 (seal sabotage) where principle-alone first registers as insufficient, and via Ch 21 where her Force-lock expertise makes her the diagnostic instrument reading Torin's counter-preparation: she sees, in the Weave, why interdiction is wrong in both senses (thematically and tactically) and does not articulate the tactical part.

arc_phase_targets.lie_reinforced: The modern Order's ignorance and the survivors' disorientation make rigidity feel justified. Sera's conditional trust in Ben during Chapter 14 ('Tell me where to stand, Skywalker') reinforces her Lie — she's following someone again because she believes they're right, repeating the Gavran pattern without examining it.
arc_phase_targets.lie_fissure: Chapter 18 (second pinch point, seal sabotage). Sera's first visible doubt about the 'principle alone is enough' framing. Not a break — a fissure. Brief, unspoken or near-unspoken: a hand pausing, a sentence cut off, a line she does not say that she would have said in Chapter 14. She also first intuits here that forcible disengagement of an entangled Force presence would accelerate the cascade — the principle that pays out at Ch 21. Two threads serviced by one beat.
arc_phase_targets.lie_questioned: Ben repeatedly proves morally serious even when tactically improvisational. At the Jedi outpost (Chapter 19), Sera watches modern Jedi suffer from Weave distortion and recognizes that principled certainty alone — being right about the Weave — doesn't protect anyone. Ben's response to helplessness (leading without controlling) shows her a kind of leadership Gavran never demonstrated.
arc_phase_targets.lie_cracking: Chapter 21. Sera reads Torin's counter-preparation in the Weave — a dead-man's trigger on his own Force presence, prepared for the interdiction options he knew the group would consider. She does not articulate it. Her Force-lock expertise is the instrument; her silence is the signature. 'I was the one they sealed. I cannot seal another.' is the articulated thematic refusal; the tactical refusal lives under the line, registered by the room without being named.
arc_phase_targets.lie_confronted: Sera must trust Ben's plan and Kael's contribution despite everything in her history warning against it.
arc_phase_targets.truth_resolved: She chooses principled flexibility and remains with Torin's diminished form without surrendering her moral core.

ensemble_cast.name: Kael Drenn
ensemble_cast.role: Wildcard, outsider perspective, essential component of the climactic solution

three_dimensions.surface: Quiet, watchful, dry humor that catches people off guard. Doesn't volunteer opinions — waits until everyone else has committed to a position and then says the thing nobody wanted to hear. Reads as detached, almost lazy.
three_dimensions.backstory_inner_demons: Didn't choose the Sith. Born on a small Sith-held frontier world during the Brotherhood's last consolidations, he was tested for Force-sensitivity during a levy sweep and taken into academy service because useful children did not stay with their families. He was trained as a conscripted adept: obedience drills, survival kata, dark-side focus exercises, battlefield triage, and the lesson that short answers were safer than visible conviction. He was never a true believer; he learned what they taught because refusal meant disposal, punishment, or being handed to someone worse. Captured by Gavran's forces, he expected interrogation or execution and instead was repurposed as one of twelve chamber-bound Force-sensitive anchors in the seal's containment infrastructure. Used as living structural rebar, his Sith-trained Force presence supplied a different resonance that strengthened the seal's coverage. His silence is not emptiness. It is barracks discipline, guilt management, and the habit of a man who survived by becoming useful to people he hated. He has spent his entire life being used by institutions: conscripted by the Sith, captured by the Jedi, wired into their infrastructure as a component. Nobody has ever asked him what he wants.
three_dimensions.action_under_pressure: Kael's instinct is to survive — find the angle, minimize exposure, keep options open, say only the sentence that changes the room. This reads as cowardice to Sera and calculation to Ben. It is actually the rational response of someone whose principles were repeatedly converted into leverage by instructors, commanders, and jailers. His flaw is passivity: he sees the pattern clearly but defaults to not engaging because engagement has only ever cost him. When he finally acts, the action should feel small, precise, and chosen rather than declarative.

weiland_arc.lie_believed: Conviction is a trap. The people who believe in things are the people who destroy everything. The safest place is outside the fight.
weiland_arc.ghost: His conscription. Being taken from his family as a child and told he should be grateful for the opportunity to serve the Sith. Then watching the Jedi do functionally the same thing with their own recruits.
weiland_arc.want: To be left alone. Genuinely. He didn't ask to be frozen, didn't ask to be woken up, and doesn't want to save the galaxy.
weiland_arc.need: To discover that choosing to care — choosing to fight for something not because an institution demands it but because he decides it matters — is the only way to stop being a tool in someone else's hand. Passivity isn't freedom. It's a different kind of cage.
weiland_arc.arc_summary: Positive change — moves from detachment to chosen commitment. Across the middle chapters, four small self-driven beats carry the interior-life texture his earlier arc lacked: Ch 7 he requests specific archive records from Desh without prompt; Ch 8 he approaches Desh (not the Force-users) with a practical observation Desh had missed; Ch 15 he approaches Torin privately in a scene Ben sees from distance and cannot hear; Ch 17 he asks the direct Torin question the group has been circling, giving Sera permission to stop defending. Each beat is brief, unexplained, monk's-vocabulary. Together they render Kael as a man actively choosing — quietly — before the articulated Ch 19 critique and the Ch 23 commitment.

arc_phase_targets.lie_reinforced: Every debate confirms his suspicion that believers weaponize conviction.
arc_phase_targets.lie_questioned: Ben, Desh, and even Sera begin treating him as a person rather than a tool or category. His own self-driven actions (Ch 7 archive request, Ch 8 Kael/Desh observation) start before anyone invites him.
arc_phase_targets.lie_cracking: The crisis makes neutrality impossible; refusal to choose becomes complicity. Ch 15 (Kael/Torin private approach) and Ch 17 (the direct Torin question) render the internal work externally.
arc_phase_targets.lie_confronted: Kael must decide whether to contribute the Sith-trained piece only he can supply.
arc_phase_targets.truth_resolved: He volunteers freely, proving that chosen commitment is different from conscripted service.

arc_phase_map.self_driven_plant_1: Chapter 7 — unprompted archive request to Desh (Kolven-era disciplinary logs or equivalent, post-R04b). Pays implicitly at Ch 19 and Ch 23.
arc_phase_map.self_driven_inversion_1: Chapter 8 — Kael/Desh observation; practical pattern Desh had missed. Establishes Kael/Desh quiet alliance.
arc_phase_map.self_driven_plant_2: Chapter 15 — private approach to Torin, Ben sees from distance. Doubles as D7 Torin counter-current. Anti-pattern: does not read as 'Kael has intel on Torin'; reads as 'two men who have both been used briefly share presence.'
arc_phase_map.self_driven_inversion_2: Chapter 17 — Kael asks the direct Torin question of the group; triggers Sera-stops-defending shift.

ensemble_cast.name: Torin Hal
ensemble_cast.role: Tragic ally, internal antagonist (second plot point turn), thematic mirror

three_dimensions.surface: Commanding presence, warm in a way that surprises people. Laughs easily, tells stories with self-deprecating humor, treats Ben with genuine paternal affection. He's the one who makes the group feel like a team. First impression is that he's the most stable of the survivors. That impression is wrong.
three_dimensions.backstory_inner_demons: One of the finest Jedi warriors of his era: not a courtly mystic, but a campaign commander who knew casualty numbers by name and made frightened soldiers laugh before sending them forward. When Gavran developed the technique, Torin volunteered to test it -- not recklessly, but from duty and from the old Jedi Lord assumption that the gifted should stand between everyone else and cost. It worked. It changed him. The Force feels different around Torin -- heavier, blurred, like damage has made its answers harder to trust. He sealed himself willingly because he could feel himself slipping toward a certainty that frightened him. A thousand years later, he wakes up and the certainty is still there. Stasis did not heal it. His warmth is real; his danger is that he uses warmth to make unilateral sacrifice feel like care.
three_dimensions.action_under_pressure: Torin's instinct is to act decisively and bear the cost personally. This sounds noble but is actually a form of control — by taking all the burden on himself, he removes everyone else's agency. Every major decision in his life follows the same pattern: 'I'll handle this so you don't have to.' It's the Jedi Lord pattern. It's Jacen's pattern. And he can't see it.

weiland_arc.lie_believed: Bearing the cost alone is what makes a true Jedi. The technique changed me, but that sacrifice gives me the right — the responsibility — to use it again when the time comes.
weiland_arc.ghost: The first time he used the technique in combat. The Force lost its ordinary resistance and, for one moment, the pressure in him went quiet. That relieved clarity -- false, costly, and unforgettable -- is what he is chasing. Not power. The memory of release.
weiland_arc.want: To use the technique one final time to seal the wound permanently, proving his sacrifice wasn't meaningless.
weiland_arc.need: To accept that his sacrifice was meaningful without needing to repeat it. That stepping back and letting others find a different way isn't cowardice. He never gets there.
weiland_arc.arc_summary: Negative (tragic) — moves deeper into the lie. His inability to let go of the pattern is what breaks him from the group. The telegraph is restructured (per D7): the reader does not reach certainty about Torin's direction at the midpoint. Torin's Ch 13 in-breach response is unreadable, not a smile. Sera keeps defending him, including to herself, through Ch 15-16. The loudest telegraph beat (the equivalent of the smile) and Sera's stops-defending break both relocate to Ch 17-18, close enough to Ch 21 that reader-certainty and the turn are within a few chapters. Counter-currents plant at Ch 8 / 11 / 15 / 18 — Torin doing things a character on the corruption trajectory genuinely would not do. Not misdirection, real ambiguity. The arc architecture is unchanged; only the observability shifts. Per B2, Torin has also anticipated the group's interdiction options at Ch 21 and prepared a dead-man's trigger on his own Force presence — a counter-preparation Sera reads in the Weave but Torin does not announce.

arc_phase_targets.lie_reinforced: Each worsening breach and each sign of Veraine's progress convinces him only sacrifice can work. Beats remain, but the narrator does not over-signal; Ben is rendered misreading Torin specifically.
arc_phase_targets.lie_deepened: Ben's collective instincts and Sera's resistance briefly offer him another path, but he doubles down on the lone-sacrifice pattern. Counter-currents at Chs 8/11/15/18 keep the trajectory live rather than predetermined.
arc_phase_targets.point_of_no_return: The resonance theory reveals a solution that would require him to relinquish authorship — he consciously rejects it. Ch 17-18 carry the loudest visible telegraph, concurrent with the Jacen pattern being named (Ch 18).
arc_phase_targets.lie_acted_upon: Torin chooses unilateral transcendence over shared uncertainty, enacting the technique alone. Counter-preparation already in place: forcible interdiction would trigger immediate cascade. His dignity is the dignity of a man who has made the decision with eyes open.
arc_phase_targets.lie_consequence: His diminished survival embodies the cost of mistaking self-sacrifice for moral authority.

voice_texture.description: Torin's warmth is load-bearing canon material — R12 flags his Ch 5-12 warmth specimens as first-order content. These lines establish the register that makes the corruption arc land; the loss must be felt. Drafting pipeline preserves the following as canonical anchors:
preserved_specimens: "You know what I love about modern Jedi? You still believe the dark side is a place you can choose not to go."
"I sealed myself because I knew what I was becoming. Stasis was supposed to hold it. It did not."

He smiled. He was always smiling by the end. It was one of the things that frightened Ben most. (Note: the 'by the end' framing relocates forward with the restructured telegraph per D7; the line itself remains canon.)
voice_texture.warmth_register: Storytelling inflection, wry historical framing, textured humanity; humor that puts the room at ease without flippancy about stakes. Post-technique register in the climax flattens to emotionally hollow articulate — still intelligent, no longer warm.
voice_texture.anti_pattern: Exposition pressure must not flatten Torin's voice in Ch 5-12. His warmth is the register the corruption breaks against; sacrificing it for information density gives the reader nothing to grieve.

three_dimensions.surface: Calm, precise, almost pleasant. Speaks like someone who has already thought through every angle. Academic quality — treats the modern era like a research project. Composure never breaks. Not in combat, not in argument. A formidable warrior underneath the intellectual refinement — Brotherhood of Darkness veterans were trained for total war regardless of specialization.
three_dimensions.backstory_inner_demons: Not born Sith — she was a Republic-world academic and archive theorist whose world fell to the Brotherhood. Forced to serve, discovered latent Force-sensitivity under Sith training, and learned faster than the people who thought conquest made them intellectually superior. She rose through capability, not cruelty: alchemy, containment geometry, ritual logistics, and the patient mathematics of how belief becomes structure. Captured by Gavran's forces and repurposed as one of twelve chamber-bound Force-sensitive anchors in the seal's containment infrastructure, she was used as living structural rebar, her Force presence drained to hold the wound shut. Her partial awareness during a millennium of stasis left her with a visceral fury that preceded intellectual understanding. She escaped the fortress weeks before the main cascade by eroding her stasis field from inside through centuries of half-conscious resistance. Her moral relationship to Veranthos is coldly exact: she is right that the old seal was a crime, and wrong because she has decided the correction may consume anyone not already trapped in her arithmetic.
three_dimensions.action_under_pressure: Veraine doesn't react — she adjusts. Every setback is data. Fights only when it advances her objective. Her flaw is detachment — she has so thoroughly intellectualized the Force that she's lost the ability to feel what it does to living beings. The wound isn't a catastrophe to her because she doesn't experience it as suffering.

weiland_arc.lie_believed: The seal is worse than the wound. Gavran's technique was a panicked battlefield act; the Order's cover-up built on living anchors was the real crime. Containment has never been mercy -- it has been fear wearing the language of mercy. The only honest answer is to break the seal and accept the transition cost of ending what the Order started.
weiland_arc.ghost:
(1) Her conversion -- the moment the Brotherhood unlocked her Force sensitivity and showed her what the Jedi had done at Veranthos, a crime her own civilization had preserved rather than confronted.

(2) A thousand years of partial awareness as an anchor, her Force presence drained to maintain a wound she was not allowed to help heal, by an Order that claimed moral superiority over the Sith who had conscripted her. Both institutions used her; only the second wrote the history.
weiland_arc.want: To destroy the seal and release the wound, accepting the casualties as the cost of ending a crime the Order chose to preserve rather than face.
weiland_arc.need: To see that some crimes cannot be ended by completing them -- that a better containment is possible, and that her utilitarian arithmetic is wrong on its own terms. She does not get there.
weiland_arc.arc_summary: Flat negative -- enters certain, exits certain. Defeated by a containment method she did not anticipate and cannot dismiss: shared-burden containment with no single prisoner, no solitary keystone, and no one person load-bearing.

voice_texture.description: Veraine's working-mind residue register — the reference for how her ledger entries, archive annotations, and recovered notes sound when Ben reads them across Chs 17/19/20/22/24. Not deliberate taunts (which cheapen her); the evidence of a working mind.
voice_texture.register: Precise, certain, intellectually restless, minimal affect. Complete grammatically sophisticated sentences. No contractions. No emotional performance. She writes as she speaks — the ledger voice and the spoken voice are continuous. What changes between contexts is the audience, not the register.
evidence_beat_rules: Entries are short — a sentence, sometimes a paragraph. Not speeches.

Each entry does one specific piece of characterization: her certainty, her containment logic, her relationship to Gavran's original work, or her reading of pressure, drainage, and scar geometry at a specific site.
Never address the reader or a hypothetical opponent. She writes for herself.
Never offer a rhetorical flourish or an editorial comment on her own certainty.
voice_texture.anti_pattern: No taunts aimed at Ben. No 'if you're reading this' framings. No breaks in register. Her working mind does not know or care who will read her notes; the reader overhears, rather than being addressed.

dialogue_register.description: Per R14, Veraine's Ch 16 pitch (and her speech throughout) operates on Socratic-adjacent questioning -- questions she already knows the answers to. Carries her dignity (she invites, she does not sell) and makes her defeat specifically hers. Her clinical register uses containment vocabulary -- pressure, drainage, scarring, stagnation, release, contamination, decay, cost, transition -- rather than abstract systems language.
dialogue_register.structure: Questions from certainty, not doubt. Intellectual restlessness expressed as what-else-might-follow-from-this rather than as uncertainty. She asks Ben or Kael a question, waits for their answer, and responds with another question that incorporates what they said. The conversation always advances toward her conclusion, but she does not announce the conclusion; she invites the interlocutor to arrive.
dialogue_register.anti_pattern: No declarative monologue. No pitch framing. She never explains her plan because she does not need to justify herself to opponents. When cornered or when the stakes cut close, her register does not warm — it sharpens into a more specific question. Curiosity is the most unsettling affect she has; use it, never replace it with intensity.

ensemble_cast.name: Desh Rolan
ensemble_cast.role: Supporting character — practical grounding, emotional anchor, GAG parallel

three_dimensions.surface: Practical, calm, dry humor. Former intelligence operative now in private security. Not Force-sensitive. Reads situations through training and instinct rather than mystical perception.
three_dimensions.backstory_inner_demons: Served in GAG alongside Ben as a teenager under Jacen Solo. Complicit in things he didn't fully understand. Carries shared shame with Ben that neither has processed. Drifted into private security work — not mercenary, but close enough that it stings.
three_dimensions.action_under_pressure: Operates. Assesses threats, manages logistics, keeps people alive. The non-Force-user who saves Force-users by doing what no Force ability can replicate — hands-on, physical, practical work.

weiland_arc.status: thinned — supporting presence, not a standalone arc. Per D5, Desh does not carry a full lie_believed → lie_cracking → new_truth progression in his own named scenes. He retains Ghost and Lie as character texture; his thematic weight lives in presence and contrast, not in lie-breaking of his own. His operational work absorbs into SP-A (Ben's practical dependence on non-sensitive operational judgment) and SP2 (his pragmatism mirrors/contrasts Kael's re-emergence). SP5 as a dedicated Desh-arc subplot is demoted to half-weight operational presence.
weiland_arc.ghost: GAG service under Jacen — shared with Ben. Retained as character texture rather than active arc fuel.
weiland_arc.lie_fragment: If I do not talk about what we did in GAG, it does not require processing — retained as the dormant pressure Ch 11 surfaces, not as an arc engine.
weiland_arc.want: To help Ben and get home safely.
weiland_arc.need: To choose to be here for the right reasons, not just loyalty — rendered through action (Ch 25 unasked volunteer, Ch 27 laugh between equals) rather than through an articulated arc progression.
weiland_arc.arc_summary: Desh is the non-Force-sensitive anchor whose contribution to the theme runs through his presence and his choices under pressure, not through a tracked Weiland arc. The Ch 11 Jacen/GAG conversation, the Ch 18 fracture-warning, the Ch 25 unasked volunteering, and the Ch 27 laugh are supporting beats in Ben's arc rather than milestones in Desh's own. His non-sensitivity is his contribution: he holds the operational frame while the Force-users lose their usual footing, and per D4 he feels unweaving not at all — which is precisely what makes him the anchor the team needs.
narrative_beats: Chapter 1 — arrives as a favor to Ben
Chapter 6 — operates in support role, professionally competent
Chapter 11 — the Jacen/GAG conversation with Ben; honest reckoning with their shared history
Chapter 18 — warns Ben the group is fracturing; reveals he cares
Chapter 25 — volunteers for the sabotage mission unasked

subplots.name: The Failing Seal — Race Against Veraine
subplots.function: Main dramatic throughline. The wound in the Force is real, the seal is failing, and Veraine is racing to exploit the crisis. Carries the central dramatic question: can Ben succeed where the Jedi Lords failed?
subplots.arc_summary: From Ben's perception of wrongness through discovery of the wound, awakening of the survivors, pursuit along the Ruusan Corridor, confrontation with Veraine, Torin's defection, and the climactic shared-burden containment (Weave-Resonance) at Veranthos. Resolved by collective action replacing unilateral control.

subplots.name: The Old War — Sera/Torin Relationship
subplots.arc_summary: Sera and Torin's unresolved thousand-year relationship — from professional tension to philosophical conflict to Torin's turn to Sera's choice to stay with his diminished form. Tests whether trust can survive betrayal and whether love can exist without control.

subplots.name: The Conscript's Choice — Kael's Identity Arc
subplots.arc_summary: Kael's journey from detachment to chosen commitment. Tests whether choosing a different path works when you have no inherited path — building legacy from nothing. His Sith training becomes the essential missing element in the climactic solution.

subplots.name: The Institutional Reckoning — GAG Shadow, Reformations Cover-Up, and Veraine as the Mirror
subplots.function: Main plot complication + thematic pressure + Jacen parallel reinforcement. Merged per D5 — Veraine's institutional antagonism is the Order's internal politics expressed through one character, and Ben/Desh's GAG shadow is the personal register of the same question. The merged subplot carries (a) Ben and Desh's shared GAG history surfacing and being acknowledged, (b) Ben's discovery and metabolization of the Reformations' true purpose, (c) his agonizing decision to withhold from Luke under crisis conditions, (d) Veraine's parallel institutional exploitation as the mirror against which his choice is tested, and (e) his final choice to tell the Order. All five strands converge on Ch 28 s2 — the office scene pays off the thread that has been running through Veraine's ledger, Ben's silences, and Desh's steady presence all along.
subplots.arc_summary: From Ben's private discovery in the fortress archive through Veraine's ledger-voice evidence in the middle chapters, through the Jacen pattern recognized in Torin, through Ben's Ch 15 withholding and his Ch 21 crystallizing realization, to Ben telling Luke everything in Ch 28. Tests the theme at every register simultaneously: personal (Ben/Desh), antagonist-mirror (Veraine), and institutional (Luke / the Order).
subplots.merge_note: Absorbs prior SP3 (Brothers in Complicity) and prior SP4 (Institutional Lie). Retains SP3 identifier for downstream cross-reference stability; scene cards and blueprints treat SP3 as the unified thread.

subplots.name: The Strategist's Game — Veraine's Operational Presence (half-subplot)
subplots.function: Half-subplot per D5. Veraine's operational activities (crew movements, amplification-array construction, infrastructure repurposing) as read by Desh through tactical evidence, separate from Veraine's ideological/institutional role (which now lives in merged SP3). Half-weight operational presence — not a full arc. Flagged for blueprint/scene-card audits to remove Desh-operational obligations where they are better served under SP-A, retaining SP5 only where Veraine's specifically-Veraine operational signature is load-bearing.
subplots.arc_summary: Veraine's practical footprint — her crew, her ship, her tactical rhythm — as visible through Corridor evidence and Desh's reads. Distinct from the SP3 merged thread (which carries her ideological and institutional weight). Delivered through site-by-site forensic observation rather than POV access.
subplots.demotion_note: Per D5, demoted from full subplot to half-weight operational presence. Many prior SP5-tagged beats migrate to SP-A (Ben's practical dependence on non-sensitive operational judgment) or SP2 (Desh's pragmatism mirroring Kael's re-emergence). Effective concurrent subplot count: four (SP-A, SP1, SP2, merged SP3), plus SP5 as half-weight operational presence.

hooks.description: The wrongness in the Force has a direction — it's coming from somewhere deep in the Outer Rim, and Ben's survey route runs directly along the bearing
The pattern of anomalous ruins with unrecognized markings on specific survey worlds — connected to the wrongness
The perimeter facility message: 'the seal is failing' — coordinates to the fortress in uncharted space

Three figures in stasis, eight dark chambers with bodies, and one chamber empty — broken open from inside, damage marks on the walls, emergency warnings in the monitoring system that went unanswered. Something got out.

The monitoring logs identify the empty chamber's occupant: a high-risk Sith-trained prisoner flagged by Gavran himself. Veraine escaped weeks ago. She's already moving along the Corridor. The race begins.
Torin's quiet question about the modern Jedi's relationship with the light/dark boundary — 'Gavran thought so too. Before.' — seeds his eventual turn
Recent markings in ancient ruins — someone has been through the Corridor ahead of them. Veraine's trail goes warm.
Torin's unsettling calm in the thin place — the unwoven Force feels familiar to him. 'Ankhural called it the natural state.'
Ship alarm — the next planned stop has been breached. Someone is there or has been there. Veraine's trail intensifies.
Desh's analysis: 'She's not just ahead — she's leading us. We're not chasing her.' Why does Veraine want them to follow?
The Maetha Facility — sealed by Gavran himself with the annotation 'Do not access without direct authorization.' Whatever happened here, even Gavran considered it dangerous.
The wrongness lurches — a sudden sharp spike. The seal is being deliberately attacked. Veraine has moved from research to action.
Veraine is heading directly for Veranthos. Based on the rate of seal deterioration, she'll arrive with enough momentum to attempt a full breach.

Gavran's archived note: 'Ankhural theorized that the Weave could be reinforced through harmonic resonance between disparate traditions. We lacked the will or the trust to attempt it.' The seed of the solution.
Torin's devastating observation: 'You're curating reality to manage the outcome you want. You know who else did that?' — naming the pattern Ben is falling into
The seal lurches again — stronger, sustained. Veraine used the truce to deliver sabotage. The timeline collapses to days.
Torin standing in the doorway: 'We need to talk about what happens when we get there.' His voice calm, warm, decided. Ben's stomach drops.
Long-range sensors detect another ship on parallel course toward Veranthos. Veraine is visible now. The convergence tightens.
Close enough to feel the primary wound — immense, pulling. Torin leans into it. Desh reports: 'She's already there.' Veraine has reached Veranthos.
Torin's expression as they approach the wound source — not certainty or determination, but longing. Ben knows the turn is coming. Hours, not days.
Torin's departure and Ben's crystallizing realization — Gavran's note about Weave-Resonance. 'I need to show you something in the Codex.'
Kael's question: 'Why should I believe this one is different?' — the final holdout before the plan can execute

The group moves toward the wound source — three Force-users and one non-Force-user, walking toward something unprecedented. Ben feels Sera's and Kael's Force presences beside him. Different. Complementary. Not yet a chord.
Ben, Sera, and Kael join hands. Three traditions. 'Now.' Ben lets go of control.
Desh disables Veraine's amplification array. The resonance has a foothold. 'Now. Everything. Don't hold back.' The three frequencies align.

revelation_schedule.what: The wrongness in the Force has a direction — it's not ambient, it has a source
revelation_schedule.impact: Transforms Ben's departure from passive retreat to unconscious pursuit
revelation_schedule.setup_required: Establish the wrongness as ambient in Chapter 1's opening

revelation_schedule.what: The seal exists and is failing — ancient Jedi military infrastructure with a warning about expiration
revelation_schedule.impact: Stakes become real — transforms survey mission into galactic-scale crisis
revelation_schedule.setup_required: Pattern of anomalous ruins established in Chapter 2

revelation_schedule.what: The fortress contains twelve stasis chambers arranged in a ring: eight dark with bodies (anchors who died over centuries), three active with living occupants, and one empty — broken open from inside. Gavran's body sits in a central chamber below, at the nexus of the anchor system. The fortress is a tomb with three living people in it.
revelation_schedule.impact: Personal stakes activate — the crisis has living witnesses
revelation_schedule.setup_required: Fortress exploration in Chapter 4, vertical descent through four levels

revelation_schedule.what: The Veranthos containment protocol predates the Ruusan Reformations, and Ben realizes the later public reforms carried a private penance/cover for what the Jedi Lords did at Veranthos.
revelation_schedule.knowledge_partition: Sera, Torin, and Kael know the pre-Ruusan Veranthos protocol, Gavran's role, and the seal's human cost; they were sealed before the Ruusan aftermath and must not speak as eyewitnesses to the public reforms that followed. Ben and Desh connect the Reformations to Veranthos from modern Jedi history and archive cross-reference.
revelation_schedule.revealed_in: Chapter 5 (First Plot Point — the FPP shock, per D8)
revelation_schedule.impact: The institutional shock: the Order's inherited account is true but incomplete. One fact detonates through cross-reference rather than survivor hindsight. Specifics — technique, wound mechanics, anchor system, Brotherhood ritual — are deferred to R04b/c/d so each lands with its own dramatic air.
revelation_schedule.setup_required: Archive access with survivors' help. Ch 5 s2 survivor-introduction + one institutional inference: pre-Ruusan Veranthos protocol later buried under post-Ruusan public reform.

revelation_schedule.what: The forbidden technique — unweaving as a specific Force-lock discipline. Not a metaphorical 'dark power' but a trained practice with a known mechanism. Derived from studying Nathema, Malachor V, Quelling of Tython, Nihil Reach experiments, Ankhural Codex, Drathul IV, Caldera Knights (lineage opens progressively across Chs 7-12).
revelation_schedule.impact: The technique named — the specific discipline Torin uses, Veraine studies, Gavran invented. Ben gains the vocabulary the narrative has been withholding. Opens the lineage thread.
revelation_schedule.setup_required: R04a established in Ch 5. First Corridor stop (battlefield node) provides archive access for the technique-specific records.

revelation_schedule.what: The wound mechanics -- what the Scar is, how it is anchored at a vergence, and why Gavran's technique created a wound that would not heal because he damaged the site where the Force was already unusually concentrated.
revelation_schedule.impact: Damage mechanics at a vergence, not a new cosmology -- the wound has a specific location, a specific anchor, and a specific reason it cannot be closed by conventional reseal. Ch 13's midpoint experience lands against this framework.
revelation_schedule.setup_required: Ankhural Codex fragment (R06) recovered/read by Ch 9. R04b established.

revelation_schedule.what: The Brotherhood Ritual at Veranthos -- why the system was built the way it was. The Brotherhood of Darkness attempted a mass dark-side ritual meant to corrupt the Veranthos vergence into a permanent wound. Gavran deadened the site to stop completion -- right about the emergency, catastrophically wrong about the cost.
revelation_schedule.impact: The tragic symmetry — Gavran is not a villain but a man who made the wrong emergency choice. Complicates Ben's moral frame: the Jedi Lords were not corrupt, they were competent people under catastrophic pressure. Feeds Ch 13 midpoint sensibility and Ch 21 refusal.
revelation_schedule.setup_required: Brotherhood outpost (Ch 10) provides forward archive access.

revelation_schedule.what: Monitoring-log analysis names Veraine — Brotherhood alchemist, flagged by Gavran himself as high-risk. She broke out from inside, weeks ago.
revelation_schedule.revealed_in: Chapter 6 s1 (moved from Ch 5 s3 per D8)
revelation_schedule.impact: The race gets a name. Tension valve after Ch 5's empty-chamber unresolved mystery. Opens Ch 6 response-quadrant.
revelation_schedule.setup_required: Ch 5 s3 ends with the empty chamber unnamed.

revelation_schedule.what: The technique's full historical lineage — Nathema, Malachor V, Quelling of Tython, Nihil Reach experiments, Ankhural Codex, Drathul IV, Caldera Knights — synthesized as the intellectual ancestry of Gavran's work.
revelation_schedule.impact: Historical depth — the technique is the culmination of thousands of years of people touching the same fire.
revelation_schedule.setup_required: Archive materials loaded from fortress, supplemented by Corridor stops.

revelation_schedule.what: Veraine's technique requires a specific geographical anchor — her amplified ritual is tied to the Veranthos vergence as the only site where her ritual can achieve full breach. The realization reframes the mission: reaching Veranthos before or after she completes her approach determines the endgame shape.
revelation_schedule.revealed_in: Chapter 13 (pieced together from Desh's chrono-drift readings and Ben's Weave-sense inside the breach zone; felt-and-understood rather than narrated)
revelation_schedule.impact: Per B1, the decision-forcing fact that reroutes the mission at Ch 14 start. Connects the midpoint experience to the Ch 25-26 climactic site in a single thread — every Attack-phase chapter from Ch 14 onward is Ben making Veranthos-approach decisions. Ben knows this at Ch 14 s1.
revelation_schedule.setup_required: R04c (wound anchoring mechanics) established Ch 9. Ch 13 breach-zone sensory work integrates the realization.

revelation_schedule.what: The Ankhural Codex's theory -- a heretical claim that the local structure around vergences is imposed rather than natural
revelation_schedule.impact: Dangerous framework for the entire conflict -- Veraine's intellectual inheritance, treated seriously but never confirmed by the novel
revelation_schedule.setup_required: Codex fragment recovered from fortress or en route

revelation_schedule.what: Maetha's warning — 'The caldera does not consume you. It replaces you.'
revelation_schedule.impact: Direct foreshadowing of Torin's fate — the most important single line in the book
revelation_schedule.setup_required: Sera cracks Maetha's archive using era-specific Force-lock techniques

revelation_schedule.what: The full breach — what complete unweaving actually feels like. Torin walks into the worst of it, stops, stands there a long time, and when he turns his face is unreadable — to Ben, to Sera, to the reader. Something happened in him; we do not yet know what.
revelation_schedule.impact: Midpoint revelation — experiential, not informational. Stakes become visceral through Ben's body. Torin's unreadable reaction is a warning the reader can feel without being able to decode; per D7 Component A, the loudest Torin telegraph (the smile) is relocated to Ch 17/18 closer to the Ch 21 turn so reader-certainty and the turn itself live within a few chapters of each other. Per D7 Component B, narrator does not over-signal Torin's direction past Ben's perception; the Ch 13 read is deliberately ambiguous.
revelation_schedule.setup_required: Thin place experiences in earlier chapters as preview. The D4 character-differentiated unweaving sensations (Ben handrail-gone, Sera architecture-slack, Torin home/relief, Kael native-language, Desh chrono-drift + grief) distributed across the scene.

revelation_schedule.what: Veraine's full philosophy -- the seal as prison, release as mercy, and the arithmetic of transition cost
revelation_schedule.impact: The counter-argument articulated at full strength. Veraine's accusation lands because history supports part of it; Sera counters with firsthand evidence and Ben hears the cost in human terms.
revelation_schedule.setup_required: Veraine established through evidence of passage in earlier chapters

revelation_schedule.what: Ben recognizes the Jacen pattern in Torin
revelation_schedule.impact: The parallel becomes explicit — Ben has seen this before and knows where it leads

revelation_schedule.what: Torin has decided to act alone — 'I'm not asking for permission'
revelation_schedule.impact: The emotional gut-punch. The group loses its strongest member. Ben must find another way.
revelation_schedule.setup_required: Twenty chapters of Torin's gradual hardening

revelation_schedule.what: Weave-Resonance -- a shared-burden containment method that distributes the seal's load across traditions so no single person becomes the prison
revelation_schedule.impact: Hope -- there is another way, and it does not require living anchors or a solitary keystone. But it still requires Kael's full commitment and has never been tested.
revelation_schedule.setup_required: Gavran's note planted in Chapter 14, Ben struggling to find it in Chapter 22's opening

revelation_schedule.what: Veraine's thesis fails empirically — the wound partially opens and produces chaos, not liberation
revelation_schedule.impact: The counter-argument answered through results, not rhetoric

revelation_schedule.what: The Reformations' true history revealed to Luke — the Order will know the truth
revelation_schedule.impact: Institutional reckoning — Ben chooses transparency over self-preservation, breaking the thousand-year pattern
revelation_schedule.setup_required: Institutional lie subplot built across the full narrative

terminology_registry.definition: Jedi Knight, protagonist, son of Luke and Mara Jade Skywalker
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Sera addresses him as 'Skywalker' until late Act 3 when she shifts to 'Ben' — marks her trust arc

terminology_registry.definition: New Sith Wars Jedi Knight, Gavran's lieutenant. Sealed as a Force-sensitive anchor against her will — told it was 'for her own protection,' actually used as structural infrastructure. Her deepest wound: Gavran didn't just silence her, he used her.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Formal speech — archaic syntax, no contractions early, gradually loosening

terminology_registry.definition: New Sith Wars Battle Master, used the forbidden technique, bears its consequences
terminology_registry.usage_notes: 'Battle Master' is NSW-era rank, not modern Order. He introduces himself with it.

terminology_registry.definition: Sith-trained conscript from NSW, captured by Gavran's forces, repurposed as a Force-sensitive anchor in the seal. Parallels Veraine — same wound (institutional conscription and exploitation), opposite response (withdrawal vs. destruction).
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Never 'Sith' as a title. Never 'the Sith.' He was conscripted, not converted.

terminology_registry.definition: Brotherhood of Darkness alchemist and strategist, primary antagonist. Captured by Gavran's forces, repurposed as a Force-sensitive anchor in the seal. Escaped the fortress weeks before the main cascade.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: She introduces herself as 'Veraine' — dropping the Darth is a strategic choice. Group refers to her as 'Veraine.'

terminology_registry.definition: Former GAG operative, Ben's friend, non-Force-sensitive
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Never described through Force-perception. He's a warm absence in Ben's Force-awareness.

terminology_registry.definition: NSW Jedi Lord who developed the technique, deployed it at Veranthos to counter the Brotherhood Ritual at Veranthos, built the fortress and anchor system, and sealed himself as the central keystone, making thirteen total anchors: twelve chamber-bound plus himself. Dead at his post after centuries, his body in the fortress's central chamber. Present through archive voice, monitoring logs, and the environmental portrait of the fortress itself.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Never appears in person — dead before the story begins. Present through archive voice (meticulous, honest, haunted) and the fortress as environmental storytelling. His final monitoring log entry trails off mid-sentence.

terminology_registry.definition: Jedi scholar (~2400 BBY), author of a heretical treatise arguing that the local structure around vergences may be imposed rather than natural
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Ghost presence. Single name only. Disappeared — possibly killed, exiled, or hidden.

terminology_registry.definition: Jedi Lord (~1200 BBY), developed caldera meditation, disbanded her Knights when she saw consequences
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Referenced through archive. Voice different from Gavran — contemplative, tragic.

terminology_registry.definition: Outer Rim world at a natural vergence, site of the Battle of Veranthos and the Brotherhood Ritual at Veranthos, location of the primary wound and seal. Once a populated civilian regional hub. Now a world that drifted rather than died -- lush, overgrown, alive, and deeply wrong. Ring structure of concentric zones: the epicenter (battlefield valley with the Scar), the city (civilian ground zero, overwhelmingly alive but growing without biological logic), the evacuation zone (milder drift, evidence of flight), and the seal boundary (a membrane felt by Force-sensitives).
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Stress on second syllable: ver-AN-thos

terminology_registry.definition: NSW military installation built into a mountainside on an uncharted world. Hub of the anchor network and Gavran's monitoring station. Four vertical levels descending into the mountain: Level 1 (Operations — monitoring systems, communications), Level 2 (Archive — records, holocrons, data tablets), Level 3 (Stasis Ring — twelve chambers arranged in a ring, including one empty/broken), Level 4 (Gavran's Chamber — central node, his body at the nexus). A tomb with three living people in it.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Never formally named. 'The fortress' in group reference.

terminology_registry.definition: The seal's infrastructure network — the route connecting anchor nodes in a perimeter around the wound at Veranthos. Each node is a failed or failing anchor site. Once served as the Jedi Lords' monitoring and maintenance route; now a trail of thin places and ancient installations. Veraine travels it ahead of the group, repurposing each node into her amplification array.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Historical lane — once vital, now diminished

terminology_registry.definition: Modified YT-series light freighter, Desh's personal vessel
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Italicized as ship name. Desh's domain. Cramped for six.

terminology_registry.definition: Era-specific term for the Force's felt structure at Veranthos and in Codex/archival vocabulary. Light and dark remain natural per Legends canon; 'the Weave' is what Gavran-era and Ankhural-era practitioners called the local structure they were trying to preserve, damage, or reinforce. 'Lattice' survives in older archive documents as an earlier translation of Ankhural's term.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Always lowercase 'w' unless starting a sentence. Era-language, not narrator-proof of objective cosmology. In-character variants ('cloth,' 'stitching,' 'work,' 'threadwork') carry speaker signal -- Gavran says 'work,' Torin says 'stitching,' Veraine quotes Ankhural's 'threadwork,' Maetha's archive says 'cloth.' The abstract term 'the Weave' is the narrative-voice canonical shorthand for this local structure; speakers reach for their own word. Do not use 'lattice' in new prose except when a character is explicitly quoting a pre-revision archive source.

in_character_variants.cloth: Archival, older — Maetha-era and earlier. Suggests woven but finished, a completed fabric.
in_character_variants.stitching: Torin and Sera — NSW-era Jedi Lord vocabulary. Suggests structural, load-bearing, where the seams carry force.
in_character_variants.threadwork: Veraine, quoting Ankhural. Ornamental on the surface, structural underneath. Signals her irony -- the thing the Order treated as nature may have been locally imposed.
in_character_variants.work: Gavran's archive voice. Plainspoken. 'The work holds. The work is holding. The work is thinner than it was.' Makes the seal sound like labor, which it was.

terminology_registry.definition: Desperate Force technique that damaged and locally deadened the Force at Veranthos in order to stop the Brotherhood ritual. It produces a wound; it does not reveal a truer universal state.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Never given a formal name. 'The technique' — deliberately vague, clinical. Never capitalize as proper noun.

terminology_registry.definition: Multi-tradition shared-burden containment that distributes the seal's load across practitioners and traditions so no single person is load-bearing. Thematic pluralism; structural rejection of living-prisoner containment.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Coined by Ankhural. 'The resonance' in practice. The older 'lattice resonance' phrasing may appear once or twice in archival quotation, but the term's meaning in-story is shared-burden containment rather than cosmological proof.

terminology_registry.definition: Sensory condition inside the wound zone -- Force-sense becomes unreliable, emotional extremes amplify, dark-side residue leaks, and the environment feels wrong. Characters may experience moral disorientation inside it; the cause is damage, not proof that morality was artificial.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Descriptive, not proper noun. Never 'destruction,' never 'de-structuring' (pre-revision term). 'Unwoven' as adjective, 'unweaving' as gerund and present participle. Character voice may use 'unmade' informally but narrator uses 'unwoven.'

terminology_registry.definition: Maetha's technique of touching the light/dark boundary without crossing. Predecessor to Gavran's technique.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Maetha's term. Torin uses it occasionally.

terminology_registry.definition: Force construct built by Gavran's inner circle containing the wound at Veranthos. Originally maintained by thirteen Force-sensitive anchors (twelve in a ring plus Gavran as central keystone) embedded as living structural components. A field expedient — combat medicine on a planetary wound, never meant to be permanent. Degraded over centuries as anchors died one by one. In cascading failure at story's start.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Always 'the seal' with definite article. Singular. The original seal used living anchors; the resonance-built seal that replaces it does not.

terminology_registry.definition: Persistent Force-wound at Veranthos caused by Gavran's technique -- a standard Legends-shaped wound with unreliable Force-sense, emotional pressurization, dark-side residue bleed, and environmental wrongness
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Lowercase. Consistent with EU 'wounds in the Force.'

terminology_registry.definition: Localized regions where the seal is weak — mild unweaving manifested as folk traditions, unreliable abilities, ecological anomalies
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Our coinage from Celtic folklore. Each has local name.

terminology_registry.definition: Ben's subjective perception of the seal's deterioration — persistent, low-grade Force distortion only he can fully detect
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Ben's personal term. Fades as he understands it. By Part 3, he perceives it as seal deterioration.

terminology_registry.definition: Heretical treatise arguing that the Force's local structure at vergences is imposed rather than natural, ~2400 BBY. Force-imbued artifact. Two known copies. Uses the term 'threadwork' in older passages and 'lattice' in the translator's footnotes -- the novel's 'Weave' is a modern rendering of Ankhural's original. Seminal to Veraine's philosophy, never confirmed by mainstream Jedi or Sith tradition.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Always capitalized. Touching provides experiential flashes.

terminology_registry.definition: Maetha's final statement: 'The caldera does not consume you. It replaces you...'
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Full text delivered once. Afterward, fragments echo — especially 'replaces you.'

terminology_registry.definition: Decisive NSW engagement where Gavran deployed the technique at maximum scale, creating the primary wound
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Never depicted directly. Known through records.

terminology_registry.definition: ~3200 BBY civil conflict on Tython — Jedi attempted to harmonize light/dark, created dead zone, final abandonment of Tython
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Our creation. Tython already declining by this point.

terminology_registry.definition: ~2800 BBY Sith experiments on captive Force-sensitives, first documented cases of beings in unwoven Force
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Our creation. 'Nihil Reach' is the region name.

terminology_registry.definition: ~1800 BBY accidental unweaving when opposing Force attacks canceled out, creating temporary formless zone
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Our creation. Accidental proof of concept. 'Drathul' rhymes with 'prattle.'

terminology_registry.definition: 1000 BBY post-Ruusan restructuring — EU canon event preserved as public reform, with this AU adding a hidden private penance/cover for the earlier Veranthos protocol
terminology_registry.usage_notes: EU canon with our added layer. The public reforms are real; the hidden Veranthos layer is later institutional concealment/penance. Survivors sealed before the Ruusan aftermath know Veranthos, not the later public legislation.

terminology_registry.definition: ~1200 BBY Force-users trained in caldera meditation, disbanded when practice's effects became apparent
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Our creation. Referenced through archive only. Cautionary tale.

terminology_registry.definition: Grand Master of the Jedi Order, Ben's father. Sends Ben on the survey mission. Present in Ch 1 (departure) and Ch 28 (return/revelation).
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Ben refers to him as 'Dad' in internal monologue, 'Luke' rarely, 'my father' in formal contexts. Never 'Master Skywalker' from Ben's POV — too distant. Sera and Torin would say 'Grand Master Skywalker' or 'your father.'

terminology_registry.definition: Ben's cousin, former Jedi Knight who fell to the dark side as Darth Caedus. Murdered Mara Jade Skywalker (Ben's mother). The Jacen parallel is a structural throughline — his pattern of unilateral action mirrors the Jedi Lords' and foreshadows Torin's turn.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Ben thinks of him as 'Jacen' not 'Caedus' — the personal name carries more weight. Never referred to neutrally; always with emotional charge. The name should feel heavy on the page every time it appears.

terminology_registry.definition: Secret police force created by Jacen Solo during the Second Galactic Civil War. Ben and Desh served in it as teenagers. A source of shared shame that enables their bond and their pattern-recognition of authoritarian drift.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Full name used once for context; 'GAG' thereafter. The acronym should feel clinical and uncomfortable — it was a real institution that did real harm.

terminology_registry.definition: Planet in the Mid Rim, site of the final battle of the New Sith Wars (Seventh Battle of Ruusan, 1000 BBY). The Valley of the Jedi is a nexus of trapped Force energy. In this AU, the Ruusan Reformations enacted after the battle were dual-purpose: public restructuring of the Republic and Jedi Order, plus private penance for the Jedi Lords' use of the forbidden technique.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Distinguish between Ruusan (the planet), the Ruusan Reformations (the political/doctrinal event), and the Valley of the Jedi (the specific Force vergence). The seal's deterioration affects the Valley in Ch 15.

terminology_registry.definition: Sith organization led by Lord Kaan during the final phase of the New Sith Wars (~1010-1000 BBY). Veraine was a member. Destroyed at Ruusan by the thought bomb. In this AU, Kaan sealed Veraine before the final battle because he couldn't control what she'd do with her knowledge.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: EU canon faction. Veraine's membership humanizes the Brotherhood -- they were an organization of individuals, not a monolith of evil. At Veranthos, the Brotherhood attempted a mass dark-side ritual meant to corrupt a vergence into a lasting wound.

terminology_registry.definition: Planet stripped of all Force energy by Vitiate's ritual (~5000 BBY). Canonical EU/TOR precedent for large-scale Force manipulation. First entry in the technique lineage — the earliest documented instance of a sentient being deliberately unweaving the Force over a wide area.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: EU canon. Referenced as historical precedent, never visited. The Nathema event is the conceptual ancestor of Gavran's technique — same principle (Force unwoven) at different scale and method.

terminology_registry.definition: Planet devastated by the Mass Shadow Generator during the Mandalorian Wars (~3960 BBY). Created a wound in the Force. KOTOR II canonical precedent. Second entry in the technique lineage — fragmentary records of the wound's properties informed later researchers.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: EU canon (KOTOR II). Referenced as historical data point. The Malachor wound is a natural/accidental precedent; Gavran's technique is the engineered descendant.

terminology_registry.definition: Era-specific security technique used by New Sith Wars Jedi to seal archives, facilities, and stasis chambers. Keyed to specific Force signatures or knowledge patterns. Sera's expertise with these locks is her primary tactical contribution — she can crack seals that would take modern Jedi years to bypass.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Hyphenated. Sera's facility with them demonstrates her era-specific value and provides natural pacing control for archive access.

terminology_registry.definition: Visible artifact at the wound's epicenter — a roughly three-meter vertical line in the air where the Force was torn and never fully healed. Not glowing, not pulsing. A visual distortion like heat shimmer without heat. The focal point of the climax: Veraine directs her ritual at it, Torin directs his technique at it, the resonance trio works in relation to it.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: The Scar is always capitalized. Visible from an angle, barely visible straight on. The seal holds the wound closed but this is where the stitches are thinnest.

terminology_registry.definition: A natural location where the Force is unusually concentrated and accessible. Rare. Veranthos sits on one. The Brotherhood targeted the site for corruption; Gavran's technique at that location created a wound that would not heal because the damage centered on the vergence itself.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Narrator default is 'vergence.' 'Nexus' and 'vergence' survive as archival or character vocabulary. Modern Jedi have language for vergences even if they do not share Ankhural's framework.

terminology_registry.definition: The Brotherhood of Darkness's operation at Veranthos: a mass dark-side ritual meant to corrupt the vergence into a permanent wound in the Malachor V / Nathema silhouette. Gavran deployed the technique to stop completion.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Narrator default is 'Brotherhood Ritual at Veranthos.' 'Inverting the Weave' survives as archival or character phrasing, especially in Codex-influenced material.

terminology_registry.definition: A Force-sensitive being embedded in the seal's stasis infrastructure as a living structural component — rebar in concrete. Originally thirteen: twelve in a ring plus Gavran as central keystone. Their Force presences provided ongoing structural energy to the containment. Most died over centuries, progressively weakening the seal.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Lowercase unless starting a sentence. The metaphor is structural engineering, not mysticism.

terminology_registry.definition: Veraine's repurposing of the anchor node infrastructure into a focusing system that amplifies her ritual at Veranthos. Each node was designed to channel Force energy into the seal; she rewires them to channel Force energy against the seal. Requires a critical mass of approximately eight repurposed nodes to function. Desh disables three critical nodes during the climax to drop her below threshold.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: The group doesn't understand what Veraine has been building until Chapter 22. The evidence was visible at every Corridor stop — they just didn't recognize the pattern.

terminology_registry.definition: One of the distributed installations in the seal's perimeter network, each housing (originally) a Force-sensitive anchor. The Ruusan Corridor connects them. Failed nodes become thin places. Key nodes visited: the Battlefield Node (Chapter 7-8), the Brotherhood Outpost (Chapter 10), Maetha's Training Facility (Chapter 12), and the Breach Zone (Chapter 13).
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Generic term. Each specific node has its own identity and name in-story.
